profile.entities: Fujiyama Power Systems Ltd (brand UTL Solar); IR: Churchgate Partners; moderator Motilal Oswal
profile.mgmt: Pawan Kumar Garg (Chairman & Joint MD); Yogesh Dua (CEO & Joint MD); Prashant Gupta (CFO); Sunil Kumar (Non-Exec Director)
profile.subseg: Solar panels (Mono PERC / planned TOPCon cells); power electronics (off-grid/on-grid/hybrid inverters & PCUs); batteries (lead-acid + lithium-ion); integrated SPGS (solar power generating systems)
profile.themes: Renewable-Integration (rooftop solar under PM Surya Ghar; ALMM-2 / DCR cell localization) — genuine. Not Data-Center / EV / Defence.

deepdive.sec: Off-grid / hybrid rooftop solar systems & residential energy storage (integrated solar-panel + inverter/PCU + battery OEM with deep distribution)

bull_bear.body:
- IPO proceeds used to repay debt → net D/E 0.85x → 0.25x. No promoter stake sale or fresh raise planned in next 12 months.
- Capex self-fundable given low leverage and ~Rs 304 cr FY26 PAT; RM inventory build is the main working-capital draw.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **BIS seizures:** 10-15 of ~500 SKUs (inverters/batteries) under BIS question; max penalty = seizure value; mgmt expects no material penalty, no impact on PM Surya Ghar eligibility or Dadri/Ratlam ramp.
- **Bawal fire:** 1.3 GW lead-acid plant suspended, cause under investigation; insured; relying on third-party supply — execution/insurance-claim risk.
- **Margin transparency:** refuses segment-wise volume/revenue disclosure (competitive reasons) — limits modeling visibility.
- **Inventory bloat:** NWC 71→83 days; ~Rs 500 cr+ of ~Rs 900 cr inventory is RM; mgmt says normalizes once Ratlam ramps.
- Rising competition (many entrants into rooftop) and ground-mounted price competition; non-DCR margin pressure + inflation.
- Execution risk on delayed inverter/battery commissioning (slipped to CY27).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, candid on operational detail (utilization, mix, BIS, fire) but guarded on segment economics. Articulate strategy: necessity-led off-grid demand, distribution relationship moat ("agreements are paper, it is relationship — 15-25 yr distributors"). Conservative-leaning guidance (50% revenue, 11-13% PAT). Some over-promotion on "proprietary"/AI themes; first full year as listed entity — execution credibility still being established.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Backward integration (cells) lifts margin, NOT revenue — TOPCon/Mono cell GW does not add top line. Revenue growth must come from system volumes.
- Inverter GW sold ~2x panel GW, yet panels are the bigger revenue/inventory line (higher Rs/watt) — explains the RM inventory spike skewed to panels.
- DCR margin upside is being deliberately competed away to grow channel — the model optimizes customer/distributor acquisition over headline margin.
- Demand is "necessity/backup" (grid instability) rather than subsidy/ROI — structurally less policy-sensitive than pure on-grid peers, a differentiator.
- Mgmt explicitly trades top-line vs margin based on capacity availability — expect margin to firm when capacity-constrained, dilute when capacity is ample (Ratlam ramp).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Backward-integration M&A: "approving the acquisition of an additional 31% stake each in Zayo Energy Private Limited and Zayo Cables Private Limited, taking Fujiyama's shareholding in both companies from 19% to 50%".
- Stated intent of that investment: "to increase backward integration, strengthen the value chain and provide greater control over components used across the Company's solar power solutions business".
- Capital is being directed into own manufacturing capacity (Ratlam panels/power electronics/batteries and the announced 1.2 GW solar cell plant) rather than any distribution to shareholders discussed in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Revenue mix (Q4, mgmt approximate): ~40% solar panels / ~40% power electronics / ~20% battery (fluctuates by geography & power-cut conditions).
- Geography: core Tier-2/3 + towns/villages (UP best state, still growing); newly focused Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Assam; south demand skews on-grid/hybrid, east (Assam/WB) hybrid + off-grid.
- Plants: Noida (integrated, largest contributor), Dadri (#2; cell + 1.2 GW panel line), Ratlam (new 2 GW integrated), Bawal (lead-acid — fire-hit, suspended).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Integrated Solar Energy Solutions Platform": "Operates an integrated business model across the solar value chain with a focus on rapidly changing customer needs", offering "end-to-end solar solutions across on-grid, hybrid and off-grid systems".
- "Strong B2C Focus with Extensive Retail Reach in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities": "Consumer focused business model with ~90% B2C revenue, offering customized SPGS solutions across high growth Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets" (SPGS = Solar Power Generating Systems).
- "Large Customer Base and Strong Brand Presence": "Sold over 1.4 million inverters over last 5 years, including 4.5 lakh inverter sold in FY26, creating a large installed base that supports demand for batteries, panels and related solutions".
- Distribution: "Presence across 25 states and UTs supported by 10,100+ channel partners"; the deck also cites 900+ service engineers who give "In-Person Sales Support to Dealers/ Shoppes".
- "Industry First" claims for "rMPPT Technology, Combo UPS, Online Solar PCU"; the innovation timeline records 2024 "Granted Patent for rMPPT Technology" and 2026 "Began manufacturing Solar Cells".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Policy] PM Surya Ghar is presented as the core demand driver: "PM Surya Ghar continues to scale residential solar adoption, With over 5 million installations still untapped, this represents close to 15 GW of incremental opportunity"; the deck lists "Two main conditions for subsidy under PMSGY" — a "DCR-compliant solar panel" and an "On-grid or hybrid solar inverter".
- [Regulation] "Government of India is considering extending the ALMM framework to solar inverters", "expected to promote domestic manufacturing, enhance supply-chain security, and reduce import dependence"; new cybersecurity/communication-protocol proposals for rooftop solar inverters are also flagged, with the deck arguing compliant domestic manufacturers benefit.
- [Import dependence] "The solar inverter, lithium batteries and BMS markets in India continue to be import-dependent, with a significant portion of supplies sourced from China and other countries".
- [Exceptional item] The deck discloses an "Exceptional Item (Loss due to fire in Bawal Plant)" of Rs. 1,436 Mn, net of tax Rs. 1,074 Mn — a plant-level loss event, not part of ongoing operations.
- [Entity naming] The filing is by "Fujiyama Power Systems Limited (Formerly Fujiyama Power Systems Private Limited)", CIN L31909DL2017PLC326513, trading as Scrip Symbol UTLSOLAR / BSE 544613 — the ticker is the retail brand, not the legal entity name.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 18.5% (+240bps); driven by material-margin gains from captive cells/batteries/electronics + operating leverage + employee-cost optimization.
- DCR cells carry higher margins but mgmt deliberately passes part to channel to win customers; non-DCR margins softening; net stance "stable to improve."
- Bawal third-party sourcing (lead-acid) → marginal margin drag, offset by top-line; spare lead-acid capacity widely available as market shifts to Li-ion.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- Revenue Q4 FY26 Rs 901 cr vs Q3 FY26 ~Rs 588 cr (+53.1% QoQ); March alone ~Rs 400 cr (peak-utilization month).
- EBITDA +56% QoQ; PAT +58% QoQ; PAT margin 11.4% (Q3) → 11.8% (Q4), aided by lower finance cost (IPO debt repayment), partly offset by higher other opex.
- Ratlam 2 GW panel line commissioned (will contribute from Q1 FY27, not Q4). New events this quarter: Bawal fire (post-quarter, plant suspended); BIS seizure of 10-15 SKUs flagged; TOPCon 1.2 GW Rs 350 cr line board-approved.
- New FY27 guidance introduced: +50% revenue, 11-13% PAT margin, Ratlam full utilization by Q4 FY28.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **FY27 revenue: +50% YoY** guidance (mgmt says easily achievable on existing 1.5 GW + Ratlam 2 GW integrated capacity).
- **FY27 quarterly shape (mgmt indicative, Rs cr):** Q1 ~900, Q2 ~800, Q3 ~800, Q4 ~1,500 (seasonality — Q4 strongest).
- **PAT margin FY27: 11%–13%** (deliberately sharing DCR margins with channel to acquire customers); EBITDA margin "sustain to improve" from ~18.5%.
- Ratlam: ~50% utilization in FY27, ~80% by Q4 FY28, peak revenue ~Rs 5,000 cr when fully utilized (target Q4 FY28).
outlook.title: Guidance (next quarter / FY27)

outlook.body:
- No formal order book (retail/distribution model; revenue cycle ~14 days from distributors).
- Demand "pipeline" = ~7 mn untapped installs under PM Surya Ghar ≈ ~25 GW incremental opportunity; China adds ~60 GW rooftop/yr as TAM proxy.
- Channel: 8,900+ partners (added 80+ distributors, 450+ dealers, 30 exclusive Shoppe outlets in Q4). Target to double channel partners over ~3 years via twin-brand strategy.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **DCR / ALMM-2 play:** 1,000 MW Mono PERC cell + planned 1,200 MW TOPCon cell at Ratlam → addresses on-grid rooftop under ALMM-2 (mandatory DCR cells for grid-connected); margin (not revenue) accretive since backward integration.
- **On-grid expansion** under PM Surya Ghar (historically off-grid-led) — new TAM, Tier-1 entry.
- **Proprietary products:** "Sigma" hybrid solar PCU (claims exclusivity); developing residential & industrial BESS systems for future demand.
- **Twin-brand strategy** to roughly double channel reach.
- **AI cost-out:** mapping service & sales processes with AI to compress opex.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: A retail-distribution-led, backward-integrating rooftop solar systems OEM whose moat is a 8,900+ channel partner network selling off-grid/hybrid backup solutions into Tier-2/3 India (necessity, not subsidy-driven), now layering on-grid + DCR cell localization to ride PM Surya Ghar / ALMM-2 — first full year post-IPO printing 72% revenue growth and margin expansion.
